paragraphs.text: Organisations which rely on the PHP programming language are being told they should install a significant software update today - or consider taking their websites offline.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: Two critical vulnerabilities with PHP, which is widely used across the internet, have been identified.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: The PHP Foundation, which supports it, is issuing updates which address them on Wednesday afternoon.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes as soon as they become available.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: The Netherlands’ cyber-security agency says it is taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities identified.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: The country’s National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation’s parliament, has become inaccessible.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: “Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated,” the NCSC said in a note.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: Japan’s national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: “PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn’t even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood,” cyber-security company Huntress said.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would “likely be a priority target” for hackers.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: “The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it.”

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker “might have already have gained a foothold”.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities “indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution”.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was “seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up”.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should “continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP”.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: PHP was created for web development. It is used on servers to implement what you see when you visit websites.

paragraphs.speaker: narrator
paragraphs.text: Not all websites use it, but it nonetheless powers a large portion of the internet.
